professionalSummary: Experienced warehouse operations planner with a proven track record in labour scheduling, dock-door management, service level monitoring, and process improvement. Holds a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification and has successfully reduced dock-to-stock times while maintaining current standard work documents.
experienceHighlights: Planned weekly labour rosters and dock-door schedules for two distribution centres, balancing inbound appointments against shift capacity in the yard management tool.
Reported daily inbound and outbound service levels to site managers and raised exception notes when carrier arrivals missed their appointment window by more than an hour.
Ran structured improvement reviews (define, measure, analyse, improve, control) on receiving-dock delays with shift leads and the site quality coordinator.
Reduced average dock-to-stock time from 9.2 hours to 7.4 hours between January and June 2024, measured from the yard management tool's receipt timestamps.
Maintained receiving standard work documents for both sites and trained new receiving operatives on them during their first week of onboarding, using the documents as the training checklist.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Dock-to-stock review pack: includes January baseline extract (mean 9.2 hours), June extract (mean 7.4 hours), method note defining receipt and put-away timestamps, and site manager's sign-off page.
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided materials establish that the candidate has performed the required planning, monitoring, and improvement activities, has a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification, and has maintained receiving standard work documents. They do not provide evidence of any other certifications or unrelated experience.

evidence.text: Planned weekly labour rosters and dock-door schedules for two distribution centres, balancing inbound appointments against shift capacity in the yard management tool.
Reported daily inbound and outbound service levels to the site managers and raised exception notes when carrier arrivals missed their appointment window by more than an hour.
Ran structured improvement reviews (define, measure, analyse, improve, control) on receiving-dock delays with the shift leads and the site quality coordinator.
Reduced average dock-to-stock time from 9.2 hours to 7.4 hours between January and June 2024, measured from the yard management tool's receipt timestamps.

Work sample: the dock-to-stock review pack, with the January baseline extract (mean 9.2 hours), the June extract (mean 7.4 hours), a method note defining the receipt and put-away timestamps, and the site manager's sign-off page.
HR verification note: the candidate's Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certificate (number GB-48213) was checked against the issuing body's public register and is listed as valid until 2027.
Maintained the receiving standard work documents for both sites and trained new receiving operatives on them during their first week of onboarding, using the documents as the training checklist.

No gaps or unsupported claims were identified.
limitations: The evidence does not cover any additional certifications beyond Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, nor does it provide information on experience with other process improvement methodologies.
